    For an editor with no snippet engine of its own: text is what is before the cursor, ending with what was just typed. mode is text, inline or display; left out, it is worked out from the delimiters in text. An as-you-type snippet is tried first, then (unless tab=0) one TAB expands, then (unless fraction=0) a/ as \frac{a}{}. Replace the Remove bytes before the cursor with Text and visit Stops in order (or hand Body to your editor's snippets).

    GET /latex/snippets — The Maths Snippets

    GET /latex/snippets
-> {"Ok": true, "File": "/notes/latex-snippets.org", "Exists": true,
    "Snippets": [{"Trigger": "mk", "Replacement": "\\( $0 \\)", "Options": "twA",
                  "Description": "inline maths", "Group": "Into and out of maths"}, ...],
    "Problems": [{"File": "...", "Line": 12, "Msg": "trigger ([a: missing closing )"}]}
GET /latex/snippets?builtin=1     the built-in set alone

    The snippets worg, VS Code and orgs latex expand type with: the rows of every table in latexSuite.snippets (latex-snippets.org) whose header has Trigger and Replacement columns, then each built-in row the file does not replace (same trigger and modes; an empty replacement takes one away). A row of yours carries File and Line. Needs features: latexSuite: on.

    GET /ledger/balance — Balances, As An Account Tree

    GET /ledger/balance?source=money.org&period=this+year&account=Expenses&depth=2
-> {"Ok": true, "Source": "money.org", "Period": "2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31",
    "Rows": [{"Account": "Expenses:Food", "Name": "Food", "Parent": "Expenses", "Depth": 1,
              "Total": [{"Commodity": "$", "Quantity": "50", "Text": "$50.00", "Number": 50}],
              "Own": [], "Postings": 0, "Children": true}, ...],
    "Total": [...], "Problems": [], "Text": "   $850.00  Expenses\n..."}

    The parameters every /ledger/ report takes:

    source a source's name, file name or path; none (or all) for every source
    block one block of an org file alone, as ob-ledger runs it: its index from 0, its #+NAME:, or line:N
    period ledger's -p in words: this month, last year, 2026, 2026-11, q3, from 2026-01-01 to 2026-04-01
    begin, end either end alone (the end is not included)
    account account regular expressions, any of which may match; not before one (or !) leaves it out
    depth fold accounts below this depth into their parent
    real only real postings
    aux use the auxiliary date=aux dates

    Rows is every account in the tree, parents first, with its total (subaccounts included) and its own postings. Text is the report as ledger bal prints it. Problems are the journal's errors and warnings, each at its file and line.

    GET /ledger/check — Problems In A Journal

    POST /ledger/check — Problems In Text Not Yet Saved

    GET  /ledger/check?source=money.org
POST /ledger/check   {"File": "/home/me/org/money.org", "Text": "* Money\n#+BEGIN_SRC ledger\n..."}
-> {"Ok": true, "Transactions": 41, "Problems": [{"File": "/home/me/org/money.org", "Line": 31,
    "Msg": "the transaction does not balance: off by $1.00", "Severity": "error"}]}

    Unbalanced transactions, failed balance assertions, dates that are not days, amounts that do not read, and (as warnings) what the reader skips: periodic and automated transactions, directives it does not know. The POST reads the text it is given - an org file's ledger blocks as one journal, or a journal when File is not an org file - which is what an editor checks a buffer with; its includes are read relative to File, and only inside the org directories. Block (an index) reads one block alone.

    GET /ledger/monthly — Totals A Month, For A Chart

    GET /ledger/monthly?source=money.org&account=^Expenses&depth=2&period=this+year
-> {"Ok": true, "Months": ["2026-01", ..., "2026-12"],
    "Series": [{"Account": "Expenses:Food", "Commodity": "$", "Values": [120, 98.5, ...],
                "Texts": ["$120.00", ...], "Total": "$1,204.50"}, ...]}

    The postings summed by month, a series an account (cut to depth) and commodity; with no depth, everything the filter takes as one series. The months run across the period when it has both ends, else from the first posting to the last.

    GET /ledger/register — Postings With A Running Total

    GET /ledger/register?source=money.org&account=^Assets:Bank$&period=last+month
-> {"Ok": true, "Rows": [{"Date": "2026-10-05", "Status": "*", "Payee": "Grocer",
    "Account": "Assets:Bank", "Amount": [...], "Total": [...],
    "File": "/home/me/org/money.org", "Line": 23, "TxLine": 20, "First": true}, ...],
    "Text": "26-Oct-05 Grocer ..."}

    The postings the filter takes in date order, each with the running total after it and the file and line it was written on. Takes the parameters /ledger/balance does.

    GET /ledger/sources — The Journals There Are

    GET /ledger/sources
-> {"Ok": true, "Sources": [{"Name": "money.org", "File": "/home/me/org/money.org",
    "Kind": "org", "Blocks": [{"Index": 0, "Name": "opening", "Lang": "ledger", "Line": 12}],
    "Transactions": 41, "Errors": 0, "Warnings": 1, "First": "2026-01-01", "Last": "2026-11-03"}]}

    Every org file with ledger or hledger source blocks, and every .ledger, .journal, .hledger and .dat file under the org directories (a .dat file only when it reads as a journal). A journal another one includes says IncludedBy, and is not counted twice when a report is over every source. Needs features: ledger:.

    GET /link/title?url=URL

    The page's title for a web address, as [[url][title]], for features: autoLinkTitle: (org-cliplink). refresh=1 skips the cache.

    {"Ok": true, "Url": "https://youtu.be/x", "Title": "Never Gonna Give You Up",
 "Raw": "Never Gonna Give You Up - YouTube", "Site": "YouTube",
 "Description": "by Rick Astley", "Icon": "https://youtu.be/favicon.ico",
 "Link": "[[https://youtu.be/x][Never Gonna Give You Up]]", "From": "oembed"}

    A url it could not read answers Ok: false with Msg and Link [[url]]; a host in autoLinkTitle.ignore adds Ignored: true.

    GET /links/all — Every Link in the Database

    Answers with every link written in every org file the server holds: what it says, where it was written, and - for a link that leaves the org files - the scheme, host and service it points at.

    This is the flat sibling of /links and /links/graph. Those answer "what points at this file" and throw away everything that is not org to org; this keeps all of it, because the links worth going back and finding are usually the external ones.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    service string no Only links belonging to this service
    file string no Only links written in this file (basename or path)

    Response: A LinkList JSON object.

    Field Type Description
    Links array The links, in file then line order
    Services array Each service and how many links point at it
    Total number How many links there are before any filter

    Each entry carries Raw, Desc, Kind, Broken, Scheme, Host, Service, where it was written (Filename, Heading, Olp, Hash, Line) and, for an org link, where it lands (ToFilename, ToHeadline, ToHash).

    GET /links/counts — How Many Places Link To Each Heading Of A File

    For features: backlinkCounts:. Every heading of the file by its zero based line, with its hash and title, and how many places link to it (Backlinks: distinct headings, a file's preamble counting as one place; Links: every link), how many links it writes to elsewhere (Out) and, with mentions, how many unlinked mentions it has (the /mentions search and its guard; MentionsSkipped says why a title was not searched). Links is every link written in the file, with its line and Col=/=End (UTF-16 code units, end exclusive) and Count, how many other links in the database land on the same heading or file (Places: written in how many other headings). File is the links to the file itself (Any: to it or any heading in it).

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    filename string yes The file.
    mentions bool no Count unlinked mentions too (slower).

    Response: A LinkCounts object. Off: {Ok: false, Off: true, Msg}.

    GET /links/counts/top — The Most Linked Headings

    Every heading in the database something links to, most linked first (by distinct places, then links). Total is how many there are before the limit.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    limit int no At most this many, default 20; 0 for every one.
    mentions bool no Count each one's unlinked mentions too.

    Response: A LinkCountTopResult.

    GET /links/heading — Links Into And Out Of One Heading

    The backlinks of a single heading, where /links answers for a whole file: every link written elsewhere that lands on this heading, and every link written under it (not under its children) that goes somewhere else. Each comes with the line it was written on, links in it shown as their text, so a list of them reads as sentences. Asked about a file instead, it answers for the file the way /links does (links within the file left out).

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    hash string one of The heading, by hash (query-escaped, not base64 again).
    filename string one of A file. With nothing else, the file is the target.
    line int no With filename: the heading this zero based line is under.
    A line above the first heading names the file.
    heading string no With filename: a heading by its text.

    Response: A LinksAround object: Target (what was asked about, with its title, id and the names mentions are searched for), In and Out, each a list of links with a Context line.

    GET /links/resolve — Where a Link Goes

    Applies the linkProtocols from the server's yaml to one link and says where it goes: a url, or a command line for the caller to run. The server never runs the command itself; it may not be the machine doing the following.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    link string yes The link as written: jira:X-1

    Response: A LinkResolution JSON object.

    Field Type Description
    Ok bool False when the protocol is not defined
    Msg string Why not
    Raw string The link
    Protocol string Its protocol, lower cased
    Url string Where it goes, for a url protocol
    Command array The arguments to run, for a cmd protocol
    CommandLine string The same, quoted for a shell

    GET /local/status — Local Runtimes for the Writing Assistant

    The local backend's runtimes (llama.cpp, LM Studio, MLX) and servers: ={Ok, Enabled, Default, CanManage, ContextLength, Runtimes: [{Id, Label, Supported, Why, State, Msg, Url, Binary, CanInstall, InstallNote, Install: {Done, Total}, Models: [{Name, Size, Params, Quant, Tools, ToolsKnown, ContextMax, Loaded}], Pulls: [{Model, Status, Done, Total, Error, Finished}], Suggested: [{Name, About, Size}], Log, CanDelete, CanCancel}], Servers: [{Name, Url, Ready, Msg, Models}]}=. State is Ollama's: missing, installing, stopped, starting, running, adopted, failed or unreachable. Asking starts nothing; a runtime is started when a model of it is used, or with start.

    GET /localimages/scan — The Web Pictures A File Links

    GET /localimages/scan?file=trip.org
-> {"Ok": true, "Count": 2, "Bytes": 812345,
    "Files": [{"File": "/notes/trip.org", "Ok": true, "Dir": "images",
               "Images": [{"Url": "https://site/x.png", "Line": 12, "Alone": true, "Sure": true,
                           "Type": "image/png", "Size": 812345},
                          {"Url": "https://cdn/photo-1501", "Line": 20, "Sure": false, "Type": "image/jpeg"}]}]}

    For features: localImages:. What /localimages/fetch would download: [[https://…/x.png]], [[https://…/x.png][desc]] and a picture's url on a line of its own (not in source, example or export blocks, drawers, headings or keyword lines). A url with no extension is a picture only when its server says so: with one file named, servers are asked (a HEAD, at most 40), which is also where sizes come from. With no file, every file is scanned and nobody is asked unless probe=1. Skip says why one will not be fetched (an ignored host, a private address). Line counts from 1. Writes nothing.

    GET /localimages/settings — Where Web Pictures Go

    POST /localimages/settings — Change It

    GET  /localimages/settings
-> {"Ok": true, "Dir": "images", "Auto": false, "MaxImageMB": 20, "MaxRunMB": 200,
    "Ignore": ["example.com"], "AllowPrivate": false, "Svg": false, "Annotate": true}
POST /localimages/settings {"Dir": "images/{file}", "Auto": true}

    For features: localImages:. The POST changes dir, auto, maxImageMB and annotate (the fields it is sent; the others are the yaml's to change) at once and in the server's yaml (server: localImages:, the file kept as <file>.before-localimages). Administrators only, unless noAuth. A dir that would leave the org directories is refused.

    GET /lsp/runnable — Which Languages A Block May Run In

    GET /lsp/runnable?lang=python&lang=dot
{"python": "", "dot": "orgs does not know how to run \"dot\". ..."}

    For each lang, empty when a block in it would run here, otherwise why not: babel off, a language it has no runner for, or one left out of babel.languages. An editor offers "run" only where a run would happen.

    GET /map/places — Headings With A Place

    Needs features: mapView:. Every heading with a :LOCATION: (coordinates, a geo: uri, a maps url, or an address), :LATITUDE:=/:LONGITUDE:=, or a record's :ADDRESS:=/:ADDRESS_<label>:= - one entry per place, so a contact with a home and a work address is two pins.

    Parameter Description
    query only the headings this query finds (IsTask(), HasTags("travel"))
    file only this file's headings
    colour keyword (default: none / to do / done) or tag (the first tag)

    Each place has Hash, Title, Keyword, Done, Tags, Filename, Line, Key (the property), Label (home, work), Value (as written), Has with Lat=/=Lon, How (coordinates, latlon, geo - written back -, geocoded - looked up and cached), Address, Found (the geocoder's name), NotFound, Snippet and Colour. An address not looked up yet has Has false; Unplaced counts them and Pending is how many are waiting for the geocoder. With mapView.autoGeocode they are queued at once; otherwise POST /map/geocode {All: true} does it.

    GET /map/static — A Map As A Picture

    Needs features: mapView:. The SVG an html export draws for a #+MAP: line (tiles composed into one JPEG under numbered pins, or pins over a grid of degrees when tiles are off or out of reach), as image/svg+xml. Parameters: query, file (as /map/places; neither = every place), or ll=49.28,-123.12 (one pin, titled title); options (a #+MAP: line's words: zoom, center, height, width, colour, tiles:nil), and width=/=height=/=zoom on their own. format=json answers {Ok, Svg, Places} instead (for a client that only speaks json, VS Code's hover).

    GET /map/status — The Map View's Settings And Geocoder

    Needs features: mapView:. What a client needs to draw the map (TileUrl, TileDarkUrl, Attribution, GeoProperty) and how the mapGeocoder is doing: GeocodeUrl, AutoGeocode, Cached / Missing (addresses in the cache, found and not), Pending (waiting their turn), Asked (lookups since the server started), LastError and LastAt.

    GET /mapgen — The Map Generator's Settings

    The settings of the map generators, for a form: each with its id, its property name in a map's org file, a label, a group, its kind (range, number, angle, select), range or choices, and which generator it belongs to (gen: terrain, hex, or empty for both). Also the kinds of terrain that can be painted, the defaults, and the kinds of place (on a region or world map, and in a town).

    Method: GET

    Response: {ok, fields, strokes, defaults, places, cityPlaces}

    GET /mapgen/names — Names for Places

    Names for places on a map, English-sounding ("Ashford", "Kingsbridge-on-Lune"), by kind.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    kind string no town (the default), village, city, castle or ruin.
    n int no How many (10, at most 100).
    seed int no The same seed, the same names.

    Response: {ok, names: [...]}

    GET /media/sessions — Every Recording With Notes

    GET /media/notes — The Notes On A Heading Or File

    POST /media/note — Add A Note At A Moment

    POST /media/start — Start Notes On A Recording

    POST /media/transcribe — Transcribe A Recording Into Linked Notes

    GET /media/file — The Recording

    GET  /media/sessions    {"Ok": true, "Sessions": [{Hash, Headline, Filename, Line, From, Notes,
                         "Media": {Kind, Link, Target, Key, Path, Exists, Online, Url, Youtube, Vimeo}}]}
GET  /media/notes?hash=...  (or ?file=notes.org)
                        {"Ok": true, "Session": {...}, "Groups": [{"Media": {...},
                         "Notes": [{Seconds, End, Stamp, Label, Text, Line, Hash, Headline}]}]}
POST /media/note        {"Hash": h, "Seconds": 750, "End": 760, "Text": "...", "Media": "optional"}
                        (or "File" + "Line" for the heading that line is in)
POST /media/start       {"File": "notes.org", "Under": "optional parent hash", "Media": "x.mp4", "Title": "..."}
POST /media/transcribe  {"Hash": h, "Model": "", "Language": "", "Write": true}
GET  /media/file?file=<org file>&path=<the recording's path>

    org-media-note's links: [[video:file.mp4#0:12:30][0:12:30]], [[audio:x.mp3#0:01:23-0:01:40][...]] (an A-B loop), videocite: / audiocite: with a citation key, and urls (YouTube, Vimeo) as the target. A session is a heading with :MEDIA:, :AUDIO: or a media link of its own. A note goes in as - [[video:…#H:MM:SS][H:MM:SS]] text among the heading's other notes on that recording, in time order; End makes it a loop. Media is only needed when the heading has no recording, or for another one. Transcribing needs the voice: whisper server; without Write it only answers the segments and the lines. Url is where a browser plays the recording: under /images when it is in the first org directory, else /media/file, which serves only a recording the org file names. Needs features: mediaNotes:.

    GET /mediadb/search — Look A Book, Film, Show, Game Or Album Up

    GET /mediadb/details — One In Full

    POST /mediadb/add — File One As A Heading

    GET /mediadb/items — What Is On The Shelves

    POST /mediadb/refresh — Fill In What A Heading Is Missing

    POST /mediadb/set — Its Shelf And Stars

    GET /mediadb/sources — Which Catalogues Can Be Asked

    GET  /mediadb/search?kind=book&q=dune[&source=googlebooks]
     {"Ok": true, "Kind": "book", "Source": "openlibrary", "Attribution": "...",
      "Candidates": [{Kind, Source, Id, Title, Year, Creator, Thumb, Blurb, Isbn, Have}],
      "Tried": [{Source, Label, Msg}]}
GET  /mediadb/details?kind=film&source=tmdb&id=movie/329865
     {"Ok": true, "Item": {Kind, Source, Id, Title, Creators, Cast, Date, Genres, Description, Cover, Url, ...}}
POST /mediadb/add  {"Kind": "book", "Source": "openlibrary", "Id": "OL893414W", "File": "", "Under": "",
                    "Status": "reading", "Rating": 4, "Force": false, "NoCover": false, "Preview": false}
     {"Ok": true, "Hash", "Filename", "Line", "Item", "Org" (with Preview), "Existing" (when refused), "Warnings"}
GET  /mediadb/items?kind=book[&shelf=doing][&about=true]
     {"Ok": true, "Items": [{Hash, Filename, Line, Kind, Title, Creator, Year, Shelf, StatusWord, Rating,
                             Cover, Tags, MediaId, Isbn, Url, Started, Finished, Fields, About}]}
POST /mediadb/refresh {"Hash": "...", "Overwrite": false}   {"Ok": true, "Hash", "Set": [...], "Msg"}
POST /mediadb/set     {"Hash": "...", "Status": "done", "Rating": 4.5}   {"Ok": true, "Item": {...}}
GET  /mediadb/sources
     {"Ok": true, "Sources": [{Name, Label, Kinds, Usable, Missing, Site, Attribution}],
      "Kinds": [{Kind, Label, Sources, Statuses: {want, doing, done, dropped}}]}

    A kind is book, film, show (TV), game, album or other (a Wikipedia entry); movie, tv and music are taken too. Books come from Open Library (an ISBN, with or without hyphens, is looked up directly) and Google Books; films and shows from TMDB with a key, else Wikidata; games from IGDB or RAWG with keys, else Wikidata; albums from MusicBrainz (one request a second) with covers from the Cover Art Archive. The kind's sources are tried in order: one without its key is skipped, one that cannot be reached is passed over, and Tried says what each answered. Answers are kept for an hour. Requests are http(s) only, 15 seconds, 4 MB (10 MB for a cover), with a User-Agent naming orgs and mediaDb.contact.

    /mediadb/add writes a record heading - :RECORD: book (film, show…), ID, ADDED, the kind's fields (AUTHOR, PUBLISHED_DATE, PUBLISHER, PAGES, ISBN; DIRECTOR, CAST, RELEASE_DATE, RUNTIME; CREATOR, NETWORK, SEASONS; DEVELOPER, PLATFORMS; ARTIST, LABEL, TRACKS), URL, IMAGE, MEDIA_ID (source:id), STATUS - with the genres as tags and the description (an album's tracks too) as its text. The cover is saved in images/<kind>/ beside the org file and linked relatively. It goes under Under in File; else the kind's file=/=under or capture template in the yaml; else the kind's collection; else a new collection heading (Books, Films…) in library.org. The same MEDIA_ID or ISBN already filed is refused unless Force.

    A heading is on a shelf (want, doing, done, dropped; for a book "to read", "reading", "read", "set aside") by its STATUS property, else its TODO keyword (done keywords are done, TODO want, any other doing), else FINISHED_DATE / STARTED_DATE. /mediadb/set writes STATUS (and STARTED_DATE on starting, FINISHED_DATE on finishing, when they are not there) and RATING (0 to 5, halves allowed; 0 clears). /mediadb/refresh looks the heading up again (by MEDIA_ID, else ISBN, else title) and fills in the fields, cover, tags and - when it has none - text it is missing; Overwrite also replaces fields that changed. Needs features: mediaDb:.

    GET /mentions — Unlinked Mentions Of A Heading Or File

    Every place a heading's title or one of its aliases (or a file's #+TITLE:) is written in plain text without a link to it. Matching is case insensitive and on whole words; links, code and src/example blocks, property drawers, logbooks, keyword lines and comments are not searched, nor is the target itself. A title made only of common words ("Notes", "Meeting") is not searched unless all is given; Target.Skipped says which names were left out and why.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    hash string one of The heading, by hash.
    filename string one of A file; with line or heading, a heading in it, as
    /links/heading takes them.
    all bool no Search for a title even when it is only common words.
    limit int no At most this many mentions. Defaults to 500; 0 is no limit.

    Response: A MentionsResult: Target, then Mentions, each with the file, zero based Line, the byte Col the text starts at, the Text as written, the Before and After of the line around it, and the heading it is under. Total is how many there were before the limit.

    GET /noter/sessions — Every Document With Notes

    GET /noter/notes — One Session's Notes

    POST /noter/note — Add A Note At A Page

    POST /noter/page — Remember Where Reading Stopped

    POST /noter/start — Start Notes On A Document

    GET /noter/pdf — The Document

    GET  /noter/sessions               {"Ok": true, "Sessions": [{Hash, Headline, Filename, Document, Url, Exists, LastPage, Notes}]}
GET  /noter/notes?hash=...         {"Ok": true, "Session": {...}, "Notes": [{Hash, Headline, Page, Y, Quote, Text}]}
POST /noter/note    {"Hash": session, "Page": 4, "Y": 0.31, "Title": "...", "Quote": "...", "Text": "..."}
POST /noter/page    {"Hash": session, "Page": 12}
POST /noter/start   {"Filename": "reading.org", "Document": "papers/x.pdf", "Title": "X"}
GET  /noter/pdf?file=<org file>&doc=<NOTER_DOCUMENT>

    org-noter's sessions: a heading with :NOTER_DOCUMENT:, and under it a heading per note with :NOTER_PAGE: (a page, or (page . y) with y from 0 at the top to 1 at the bottom). A new note goes in page order under the session; Y is optional. Needs features: noter:. The pdf is served only for a session that names it, and only a .pdf.

    GET /notifications — What the Watches Found

    The logged-in user's notifications from watched queries, newest first, the last fifty kept.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    unread bool no Only those not yet marked read.
    limit int no At most this many.

    Response: A NoticeList: unread and total (counted before unread=/=limit), and notices, each with id, watch, label, at, count (matches now), read, and gained / left headings (key, headline, status, file, line, hash, path).

    GET /notify/status — How This Server Notifies

    What a notification from this server does: whether a notify plugin is configured, how this machine shows a notification (Backend, e.g. macOS (terminal-notifier)), whether it pops here (Desktop), the quiet hours and whether they are on now, the reminder times, the deadline digest time, sound, focus announcements, and where a click goes (Open).

    Method: GET

    Response: A NotifyStatus JSON object.

    GET /ollama/status — Ollama for the Writing Assistant

    Whether Ollama is installed and running for the writing assistant's ollama backend, and its models: ={Ok, Enabled, State, Msg, Version, Url, Binary, CanManage, CanInstall, Install: {Done, Total}, ContextLength, Models: [{Name, Size, Family, Params, Quant, Tools, Thinking, Vision, ContextMax, Loaded}], Pulls: [{Model, Status, Done, Total, Error, Finished}], Suggested: [{Name, About, Size}], Log}=. State is missing, installing, stopped, starting, running (started by orgs), adopted (already running), failed or unreachable. Asking starts Ollama when it is installed and not running (a local url only).

    GET /pandoc — A File In Any Format Pandoc Writes

    GET /pandoc?filename=/path/notes.org&to=docx answers with the file converted by pandoc: docx, odt, epub, pptx, rst, mediawiki, asciidoc, plain and the rest. Its own endpoint, as /pdf is, because most of these are bytes rather than text. Uses the pandoc exporter's settings when one is configured, and pandoc on the PATH otherwise.

    GET /pdf — A File, Run Through LaTeX and Served as a PDF

    Exports one org file with the pdf exporter and answers with the pdf itself rather than with a path to it or a string. This is what the file view reads to show a #+LATEX_CLASS: dndbook file as the book it is asking to be.

    The result is cached against what the file was when it was built - its path, modification time and size - so opening the same book twice runs pdflatex once. Editing the file invalidates that on the next request, because the key changes with it.

    The pdf exporter must be enabled in the server's config under server.exporters, and pdflatex must be installed; without either, the answer is a 500 saying which.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    query string yes The org file to export (basename or path)
    refresh string no t to rebuild even when the cache has it

    Response: application/pdf on success; text/plain with the reason and a 500 otherwise.

    GET /plan/day — The Day Planner: Blocks, Tasks to Place, and Load

    One day laid out for time-blocking: the timed things already on it, the open tasks that could go on it, and how full it is inside the working window. worg's Agenda day view and orgs plan draw this.

    • Blocks are the day's timed agenda entries (a SCHEDULED, a plain stamp, a deadline with a time), each with Start=/=End as HH:MM. A stamp with no end is given its EFFORT, else an hour (Implied). A deadline is a moment (Mins 0). Movable is true for a one-day SCHEDULED that is not done: the planner's to move, resize and unplan.
    • Tasks are what the query finds (default IsTask()), less anything done, archived, commented, a habit, already on the day with a time, or scheduled after the day. Scheduled on or before the day without a time comes first, with Late days. EffortMins sizes a drop.
    • AllDay is the rest of the day's entries without a time.
    • Load counts minutes inside the window covered by a block (PlannedMins), left (FreeMins), covered twice (DoubleMins), and the backlog's EFFORT. Overlaps are pairs of indexes into Blocks.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    date date no The day, YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to today.
    query string no The tasks to offer, as /search. Default IsTask().
    dayStart time no The working window's start, HH:MM. Default 09:00.
    dayEnd time no Its end. Default 17:00.
    today date no The day to count late from. The server's date.

    Response: A PlanDay: ={"Ok": true, "Date", "Today", "DayStart", "DayEnd", "Query", "Blocks": […], "AllDay": […], "Tasks": […], "Load": {…}, "Overlaps": i, j, "DefaultMins": 60}=, or Ok: false with Msg.

    POST /plan/block — Place a Heading on the Day

    Writes SCHEDULED: <2026-10-12 Mon 10:00-11:00> on the heading, as a line edit of its planning line. A repeater or warning already on its SCHEDULED is kept. Moving and resizing a block is the same call.

    Method: POST

    Request Body (JSON):

    Field Type Required Description
    Hash string yes The heading.
    Date string no YYYY-MM-DD; today when empty.
    Start string no HH:MM. Empty: the first free gap long enough (from now today).
    End string no HH:MM. Empty: Start plus EFFORT, else an hour.
    DayStart string no The window the free gap is looked for in. Default 09:00.
    DayEnd string no Default 17:00.

    Response: A PlanWrite: {"Ok": true, "Hash", "Stamp", "Start", "End"}, or Ok: false with Msg.

    POST /plan/unblock — Take a Heading off the Day

    Removes SCHEDULED from the heading. On a repeating SCHEDULED, or with KeepDate, only the time comes off: the date and repeater stay.

    Method: POST

    Request Body (JSON):

    Field Type Required Description
    Hash string yes The heading.
    KeepDate bool no Keep the date, take off the time.

    Response: A PlanWrite; Stamp is what is left, empty when SCHEDULED was removed.

    GET /preview — What A Link Points At (hover previews)

    For features.hoverEditor. Resolves a link as it is written in an org file and answers what it points at, for a hover card: a heading (id:…, *Title, Title, x.org::*Title, x.org::#custom-id), a whole file (x.html), lines of one (x.org::42), a picture, a pdf, a recording, a web page or a linkProtocols link.

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Required Description
    link yes The link, with or without its brackets and description
    from no The org file it is written in; relative links and *Title are read against it

    Response: a Preview:

    Field Description
    Kind heading, file, text, source, image, pdf, media, web, command
    Title, Todo, Tags, Path The heading's title, keyword, tags and the headings above it
    Html The text rendered by the html exporter (a heading without its own line, planning and drawer)
    Text, File, From, To The org text and the rows (0 based) it is in
    Base A hash of Text and its neighbouring lines, which /preview/save checks
    Editable Whether /preview/save will take it
    Hash The heading's hash, for the other endpoints
    Url Where a picture, pdf, recording or page is fetched
    Description, Image, Site A web page's own, from its meta tags

    Refused while the feature is off.

    GET /query/explain?query=Q

    What a query becomes before it runs: Full is a short query translated into the full form, Expanded that with its {{ filters }} written in. Ok is false, with Msg, when it would not parse. What orgs search -explain shows.

    GET /recap — What Happened, and What Is in the Way

    The material of orgs standup and orgs recap, in one walk over every heading that is not archived or under a COMMENT heading.

    Parameters: from and to (YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive), or block (a clock table range: today, yesterday, thisweek, lastweek, thismonth, 2026-W40…). Without them, the last seven days, today included. today (YYYY-MM-DD) moves "today" for the today-shaped parts.

    Response: A Recap:

    • Closed: headings finished in the range, newest first: a CLOSED in it on a finished keyword, or a State "DONE" logbook line in it (so a repeating task, put back to TODO the moment it is done, still counts). Count is the distinct days, Repeat marks a repeating one, Cancelled a cancelling keyword. Habits go to Habits instead.
    • Clocked: minutes of every clock line inside the range (a running one to now), by the nearest project at or above the heading, else by file; ClockedMins the whole of it. Running is a clock with no end.
    • Agenda: today's agenda, unfinished and not habits (Kind scheduled, deadline, timestamp, overdue), then NEXT tasks not already in it (next).
    • Waiting: the weekly review's waiting list, longest first, with Days and SinceFrom read the same way.
    • Blocked: the blocked-chain, ordered-stuck and waiting-on-done problems of /insights/deps.
    • Habits: each habit with the days it was done in the range.
    • Writing: words written in writing mode (End - Start per day of the writing log), the days with words, and the goal that fits the span (weekly for seven days, monthly for a month, else daily times days).

    Headlines are plain text: emphasis markers gone, a link as its description, timestamps and cookies left out.

    GET /record/{hash} — One Record

    The record that heading is, with its notes and its update history. Answers with an error rather than an empty record when the heading is not one.

    GET /records — Find Records

    Answers with every record, or with the records of one collection.

    Parameter Meaning
    type Only this collection: contact, equipment. All when empty
    q Only records matching this text anywhere in them
    body 1 to include the notes and the history

    A record's fields come back parsed - name, label, kind and an actionable link - so a client draws a contact and a guitar pedal with the same code.

    GET /records/birthdays — Birthdays In A Window

    ?from=2026-09-01&to=2026-09-30 answers with every birthday and anniversary falling in those dates, worked out from the day each record says the thing started. Both are optional: the default window is the next year from today.

    The occurrence is worked out here rather than in the client, so the agenda, the CLI and anything else asking get the same answer - including the 29th of February, which is kept on the 28th in a year that has no 29th.

    GET /records/collections — What Collections Exist

    Every collection the database knows about: the ones with a container heading and the ones that exist only because records carry the type, with how many records each holds and where new ones would be filed.

    GET /records/fields — The Fields A Collection Uses

    ?type=contact answers with the field names records of that type carry, the collection's own FIELDS first and the rest by how many records use them. This is what an add form offers before anything has been typed.

    GET /recur — Every Heading With An org-recur Rule

    GET /recur?n=3
-> {"Ok": true, "Weekdays": "mon,tue,wed,thu,fri", "Items": [{"Hash": "...",
    "Headline": "Water plants", "Title": "Water plants |+2|", "Filename": "...",
    "Line": 12, "Status": "TODO", "Rule": "+2", "Words": "every 2 days",
    "Stamp": "SCHEDULED", "Current": "<2026-11-04 Wed>", "Next": "2026-11-06 Fri",
    "Upcoming": ["2026-11-06 Fri", "2026-11-08 Sun", "2026-11-10 Tue"]}]}

    Every heading whose title has |...| in it (features: recur:). Next is where marking it done today moves its Stamp; Upcoming the next n (default 3, at most 20) dates if it is done on each. Bars holding something that is not a rule come back with Err and no dates. Only headings in an open keyword (or none) are listed, unless all=1.

    GET /recur/explain — What An org-recur Rule Means

    GET /recur/explain?rule=|1,15|&n=4
-> {"Ok": true, "Rule": "1,15", "Words": "the 1st and 15th of each month",
    "Next": ["2026-11-15 Sun", "2026-12-01 Tue", "2026-12-15 Tue", "2027-01-01 Fri"]}

    The rule's next n dates (default 5, at most 50) from today, each one where done on the one before it moves the heading. The bars are optional. A rule that does not read answers Ok: false and why. Works with features: recur: off - it only reads.

    GET /refactor/lists — The Lists In A Heading's Text

    The plain and checkbox lists written in one heading's own text (not its children's), for choosing which one /refactor/list should turn into headings.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters: hash, the heading.

    Response: {Ok, Msg, Lists: [{Line, End, Items, First, Checkboxes}]}, Line and End zero-based rows of the file.

    GET /refactor/tags — Every Tag In Use, For Renaming

    Every tag written anywhere: on headlines, in #+FILETAGS: lines, and defined on #+TAGS: lines, with how many headlines and files carry it. Read off the files' own lines, most used first.

    Method: GET

    Response: {Ok, Msg, Tags: [{Tag, Headings, Files, Defined}]}.

    GET /reformat — What Reformatting Would Change

    Answers with the text the org writer would produce for a file, and whether that is already what is on disk - without writing anything. The POST of the same path does the write; this is the same question asked without doing it, which is what a pre-commit hook or a CI step needs.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    filename string yes The org file to check.
    text string no Set to f to leave the formatted text out of the answer.

    Response: A ReformatCheck JSON object.

    {"Ok": true, "Formatted": false, "Text": "* TODO Something\n"}

    GET /refresh — What Is Kept Current, And How It Went

    Everything on a timer: source blocks and #+CALL: lines with :schedule, dynamic blocks with :refresh, and files with #+REFRESH: (or every file with a dynamic block or a table formula, under refresh.every). Each item says what it is (Kind, File, Line, Name), how often and who said so (Every, From), when it last ran and will next (Last, Next), how that went (Ok, Msg, Changed, Millis), and why it will not run, if it will not (Blocked: babel is off, a schedule that does not read).

    GET /related — Notes Like This One

    The headings most like a heading (its whole subtree) or a file (features.related). Left out: the heading itself, its ancestors and descendants (a file: everything in it), and anything a link already joins to it either way.

    Parameter Type Required Description
    hash string or file The heading.
    file string or hash A file (filename also works); with line the heading that zero-based line is in.
    n int no How many (default 10, at most 100).
    engine string no words or embeddings (default related.engine, auto).
    linked bool no Keep results already linked, marked Linked.

    Response: RelatedResult: Engine (the one that answered), Target, Items (Hash, Filename, Olp - its parents -, Headline, Line, Score 0-1, Words=/=Embed the two engines' parts, Terms the words they share most, Snippet the sentence most like the target, Linked), Skipped (already linked and left out).

    GET /related/pairs — Alike, And Not Linked

    Pairs of headings across the database most like each other with no link between them either way, best first: Pairs of {A, B, Score} (B has the shared Terms and a Snippet). n (default 30, at most 200). Found by words, re-scored by embeddings when they are ready.

    GET /related/status — How Related Notes Stands

    How many headings the words engine holds, the engine a question gets by default, and the embeddings engine's progress: Configured, Backend, Model, State (off, idle, embedding, waiting, error), Total, Done, Pending, LastError, Store (the vectors file).

    GET /remark/sources — Every File And Page With Highlights

    GET /remark — One Source's Highlights

    POST /remark/highlight — Highlight A Passage

    POST /remark/note — Change A Highlight's Note

    POST /remark/delete — Take A Highlight Away

    GET  /remark/sources              {"Ok": true, "NotesFile": "...", "Sources": [{Source, Title, Url, Count}]}
GET  /remark?source=<path or url> {"Ok": true, "Highlights": [{Id, Beg, End, Label, Text, Note, Line, Col, EndLine, EndCol, Moved, Lost}]}
POST /remark/highlight  {"Source": "...", "Beg": 120, "End": 141, "Text": "the words", "Label": "", "Note": ""}
POST /remark/note       {"Id": "9f2c41aa", "Note": "..."}
POST /remark/delete     {"Id": "9f2c41aa"}

    org-remark's marginalia file (remark: notesFile:, default marginalia.org in the first org directory). Positions are characters counted from 1 with the end exclusive, as Emacs counts them. A highlight whose file has changed is found again by its words (Moved); one whose words have gone is Lost. A highlight with no Beg is placed at the first occurrence of Text at or after Line (0 based). Needs features: remark:.

    GET /review/inbox — The Inbox, One Item Per Heading

    What inbox triage works through: the headings the review.inbox query finds (by default the top level of every file called inbox.org that is neither archived nor done). Only the outermost heading a query finds is an item - what is under it goes wherever it goes, and is counted in Children.

    Method: GET

    Response: A ReviewList: Ok, Msg, the Query used, and Items, each a Todo (headline, tags, hash, keyword, file, line…) plus Olp (the outline path above it), Body (the prose under it, drawers and planning taken off, cut at forty lines), Children, Effort and Scheduled.

    GET /review/last — When the Weekly Review Was Last Done

    The user's review record: State.last (when the last review was finished, RFC 3339), State.step and State.started (a review in progress, so it can be resumed where it was left, from worg or the terminal), and State.history (the last twelve, each with its summary). DaysAgo is whole days since the last one, -1 for never. Kept in the per-user extensions file.

    Method: GET

    Response: ReviewLast.

    GET /review/someday — The Someday Pile

    What the someday sweep works through: every heading on one of review.somedayKeywords (SOMEDAY, MAYBE) or carrying one of review.somedayTags (someday, maybe), not archived and not done. Outermost only, as for /review/inbox, so a tagged project is one item.

    Method: GET

    Response: A ReviewList, as /review/inbox.

    GET /review/weekly — The Weekly Review's Lists

    Everything the weekly review wizard asks about between emptying the inbox and the someday sweep, in one answer:

    • Stuck: projects with no NEXT action (IsBlockedProject()), each with the open tasks directly under it, any of which could be made NEXT.
    • Waiting: the review.waiting items that have waited at least waitingDays days. How long is read from org's own logbook line (State "WAITING" from ... [stamp]), else the heading's CREATED property, else its date; SinceFrom says which, and Days is -1 when nothing does. A chase (a note starting "Chased") restarts the count.
    • Time: the week's clocked minutes against its planned minutes (the EFFORT of tasks scheduled or due in it), per project (or file, outside any project) and per tag.
    • Stale: open headings scheduled before today with no clock, state change or note since the day they were scheduled for. Habits and waiting items are left out.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Required Description
    waitingDays no Override review.waitingDays (7).
    week no The week to compare, as a clock table block: lastweek (default), thisweek, 2026-W40.

    Response: A WeeklyReview.

    GET /reviews — Headings Due For Review (org-review)

    POST /reviews/mark — Mark A Heading Reviewed

    POST /reviews/set — Set A Heading's Review Cadence

    POST /reviews/snooze — Put A Review Off

    GET  /reviews?within=7        {"Ok": true, "Today": "2026-11-04", "Due": 3,
                               "Items": [{Hash, Headline, Filename, LineNum, Olp, Body, ...,
                                          Due, Late, IsDue, Last, Next, Delay, DelayFrom, Why}]}
POST /reviews/mark            {"Hash": "...", "Date": "", "Note": "still on track"}
POST /reviews/set             {"Hash": "...", "Delay": "+2w"}   ("" takes it off)
                              {"Hash": "...", "Next": "fri"}    {"Hash": "...", "Clear": true}
POST /reviews/snooze          {"Hash": "...", "Until": "+1w"}

    A heading takes part when it has :LAST_REVIEW:, :NEXT_REVIEW: or a :REVIEW_DELAY: of its own. It is due on its NEXT_REVIEW, else on LAST_REVIEW plus its delay (REVIEW_DELAY inherited from the headings above or #+PROPERTY:, else orgReview.delay, +1m). One with only a delay has never been reviewed and is due now. Archived, commented and finished headings are left out.

    GET /reviews answers what is due today or before, most overdue first; within=N adds what falls due in the next N days (Late is negative for those), all=t every heading in review. Late is days past Due; Due is empty for one never reviewed.

    /reviews/mark writes LAST_REVIEW (Date, default today, a typed date like yesterday) and NEXT_REVIEW = that day + the delay, as orgReview.setsNext says; a Note goes into the log drawer. /reviews/set with a Delay also moves NEXT_REVIEW to LAST_REVIEW (or today) + the delay. /reviews/snooze moves only NEXT_REVIEW (+1w by default, from today). Each answers {Ok, Msg, Hash, Item} with the heading as it now stands. All need features: review:.

    GET /site — A Folder of Org Files as a Static Web Site

    GET /site?dir=blog&theme=paper answers with a zip of a whole web site made from every org file under dir (relative to the first org directory or absolute inside one; dir.= is all of it): a page per file, a home page (the folder's index.org, or one made from its dated posts and pages), tag pages, an archive, backlinks, an Atom feed.xml, a sitemap.xml (with a base url), a 404.html and a search box that works with no server. Every link is relative, so the site works opened from disk or served from any path.

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Description
    dir the folder to publish
    theme paper, ink, tufte, garden, docs, mono or journal (default paper, or site.yaml's)
    drafts t publishes files marked #+DRAFT: t too
    base the url the site will live at, for the feed and the sitemap
    title the site's title (default site.yaml's, else the folder's name)
    local t writes the site on the server's disk at out instead
    out with local=t: the folder to write into
    list t answers {"Ok": true, "Themes": [{"Name", "Description"}]}

    A site.yaml in the folder sets title, description, author, baseURL, theme, language, footer, feedItems and nav (a list of {title, url}). Per file: #+TITLE, #+SUBTITLE, #+DATE (makes it a post), #+AUTHOR, #+DESCRIPTION, #+FILETAGS, #+WEIGHT (order in the navigation) and #+DRAFT. Headings tagged noexport and COMMENT subtrees are left out; linked pictures and files are copied in (only from inside the org directories).

    Response: the zip, with X-Orgs-Pages, X-Orgs-Theme and an X-Orgs-Warning header per link that leads nowhere on the site; with local=t a ResultMsg.

    GET /slides/themes — List Presentation Themes

    Returns the themes the four presentation exporters can render a deck with. A theme is a slides_theme_<name>.css file in your template folder, and the same file works in all four - reveal.js, impress.js, WebSlides and deck.js - because what it sets is a palette and a type scale rather than one library's class names.

    Any of these names can be given to /file/revealjs (or impressjs, webslides, deckjs) as theme=<name>, which overrides the #+REVEAL_THEME: the file itself asks for. A name that is not in this list is passed through to the framework, so reveal's own dracula and deck.js' swiss still work.

    Method: GET

    Parameters: None.

    Response: {"Ok": true, "Themes": ["blueprint", "bloom", "graphite", ...]}

    GET /starmap — The Database as a Galaxy

    Answers with every file or heading the server holds as a star, every link between two of them as a thread, and - at heading scope - the outline as its own kind of edge.

    This is not /links/graph with more fields on it. The graph is built out of the link index, so a heading nothing links to is not in it at all, which in a real org database is most of them; a galaxy has to hold every star. It also carries what only the server can answer: how big each thing is, when it was born, and whether it has been archived.

    Archived files and headings are never stars. They are counted in Swallowed and the most recent few are named in Eaten, which is what a client draws as the black hole's diet.

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    scope string no heading (the default) makes every heading a star, with its file as
    a hub star and the constellation it belongs to. file draws one star
    per file, grouped by its top level folder.
    query string no An org query expression every heading star has to satisfy. File stars
    are never asked - a file that failed it would take its whole
    constellation with it.
    exclude string no Comma separated folder or file names to leave out
    nologs string no t to leave out journal, daily and session stars
    limit number no Stars to hand over (default 4000, capped at 20000)

    Response: A StarmapResult JSON object.

    Field Type Description
    Ok bool False when the query does not parse
    Msg string Why it does not parse
    Scope string The scope that was used
    Nodes array The stars
    Edges array The threads, each Kind either link or outline
    Total number How many stars matched before limit was applied
    Truncated bool Whether it was
    Swallowed number Archived files and headings, which are never stars
    Eaten array The most recently archived, by name
    SkippedLinks number Links with no far end to draw in this scope

    A star carries Id ("file:<path>" or "node:<hash>", the same name spaces the link graph uses), Kind, Label, Filename, Hash, Olp, Level, Parent, Line, Folder, File, Path, Group (note or log), Size, Lines, Date, Dated, Touched, Status, Tags, In and Out.

    Folder and File are the two things a constellation can be made of, and neither is called the constellation: which one is right depends on the database rather than on the data - one folder of thirty files wants the file, four hundred day pages under journal/ want the folder - and nothing here can tell which somebody is looking at. The client decides.

    Dated says the date was written - a CREATED property, a date at the front of the name, a CLOSED stamp - rather than read off the filesystem. A modification time moves whenever anything is edited, so a client marking recent things has to know which it has.

    GET /status — The Todo Keywords This Server Accepts

    The keywords from defaultTodoStates in the server config, split the way org splits them: everything before the | is a state a task is still in, everything after it is a state it has finished in. A file with its own #+TODO: line overrides these for its own headings - use /status/{hash} to ask what one particular heading may be set to.

    Method: GET

    Response: {"Active": ["TODO", ...], "Done": ["DONE", ...]}

    The order is the order they were configured in, which is the order they are meant to be read in.

    GET /status/{hash} — Get Valid Status Keywords for a Heading

    Returns the list of valid TODO status keywords that can be applied to the heading identified by the given hash. This takes into account both the global defaultTodoStates / defaultNextStates from server config and any file-level #+TODO: or #+SEQ_TODO: definitions.

    Method: GET

    Path Parameters:

    Parameter Type Description
    {hash} string Base64-URL-encoded hash of the heading.

    Response: A JSON array of valid status keyword strings (e.g. ["TODO", "NEXT", "DONE"]), or an error string.

    GET /table — Get One Table

    Returns the full contents of a single table: its rows, its formulas, and a map telling you which formula writes which cell so an editor can show the formula of the selected cell.

    Method: GET

    Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    filename string yes The org file holding the table.
    id int yes Ordinal of the table within the file, from zero.

    Response: A TableResult JSON object. Table.Data holds one entry per line of the table, each either a "data" row with its cells or a "sep" row standing for a |---+---| rule. Table.CellFormulas is keyed by "row,col", both zero based, indexing into Table.Data.

    GET /tables — List All Tables

    Returns a summary of every table in every org file the server has loaded, in document order. A table is identified by its Filename and its Id, the ordinal of the table within that file. Both are what the other table endpoints take.

    Method: GET

    Parameters:

    Parameter Type Required Description
    filename string no Only list the tables of this org file.

    Response: A TableListResult JSON object:

    {"Ok": true, "Msg": "", "Tables": [
  {"Id": 0, "Filename": "/org/budget.org", "Name": "expenses", "Heading": "Money/Budget",
   "Olp": ["Money", "Budget"], "Line": 12, "Rows": 6, "Cols": 3, "Formulas": 2}]}

    GET /timeline/events — Dated Headings As Events

    GET /timeline/list — Every #+TIMELINE: Line

    GET /timeline/svg — A Timeline As A Picture

    GET /timeline/date — How A :DATE: Reads

    GET /timeline/events?query=HasTags(%22history%22)&group=tag&from=-500&to=1500
    {"Ok": true, "Group": "tag", "S": -77914137600000, "E": ...,
     "Events": [{"Title": "Battle of Hastings", "Kind": "point", "Source": "date",
                 "Start": "1066-10-14", "End": "", "S": -28502755200000, "E": 0,
                 "Precision": "day", "Label": "14 Oct 1066", "Lane": "england",
                 "Colour": "#2a78d6", "Slot": 0, "Hash": "...", "File": "...", "Line": 12,
                 "Keyword": "", "Tags": ["england"], "Snippet": "William of Normandy ..."}, ...],
     "Lanes": [{"Name": "england", "Colour": "#2a78d6", "Slot": 0, "Count": 14}, ...]}
GET /timeline/list   {"Ok": true, "Timelines": [{Filename, Line, Options, Block, Title, Hash, Headline}]}
GET /timeline/svg?line=group:tag from:1900&width=960     image/svg+xml
GET /timeline/date?text=c. 1200
    {"Ok": true, "Start": "1200", "S": ..., "Until": ..., "Precision": "year", "Approx": true, "Label": "c. 1200"}

    line is what follows #+TIMELINE:; query, group, from, to, file, title, clocks as parameters go on top of it, and here is the file the line is in (a line with no query: draws its own file). With neither, every dated heading in every file is an event (the most recent 2000, Truncated saying when there were more; limit changes it). S=/=E are positions: milliseconds of the date's wall-clock fields read as UTC (never an instant), astronomical years (-0043 is 44 BC), so a client draws them without a time zone. Kind is point, span or era (eras have no lane; they are drawn behind every lane). Source is where the date came from: date (the :DATE: property), range (an org date range), planned (SCHEDULED to DEADLINE), timestamp, closed, scheduled, deadline, created, datetree, clock. Slot is the lane's place in the chart palette, -1 for a heading's own :COLOR: or a lane past the eighth. /timeline/date reads a free date as :DATE: does, for an editor's hover. Needs features: timeline:.

    GET /timer, POST /timer — The Relative Timer

    POST /timer/item — A Note Stamped With It

    POST /clock/resolve — Idle Time On The Running Clock

    GET /timer is {Ok, Running, Paused, Countdown, Elapsed, Remaining, Display, Started}. POST /timer takes {"Op": "start"} (or pause, continue, stop, {"Op": "countdown", "Minutes": 25} - a notification when it ends -, {"Op": "set", "Offset": "0:10:00"}) and answers the state.

    POST /timer/item {"Hash": "...", "Text": "they agreed"} writes - 0:03:12 :: they agreed at the end of the heading's own text (the clocked heading when Hash is empty), straight after the last such item.

    POST /clock/resolve {"How": "subtract", "Minutes": 20} takes idle minutes off the running clock; "stop" clocks out that long ago; "keep" does nothing. GET /clock/idle is {Minutes}, the yaml's clockIdleMinutes (0 is off).

    GET /timesheet — Clocked Time by Client, as a Timesheet or Invoice

    Every CLOCK line in a range, attributed to a client and priced (see Timesheets and Invoices for how a client is decided). Answers json by default; format=csv or format=html with kind=timesheet (a row a sitting) or kind=invoice (a row an invoice line, one invoice per client).

    Method: GET

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Description
    block the range, as a clock table writes it (lastmonth, 2026-W41, …)
    tstart, tend the range's edges as dates, narrowing or replacing block
    by client (default), tag, project, file
    tags with by=tag, the tags that are clients, comma separated
    client only this client
    rate an hour, where neither heading nor client says
    round minutes each line is rounded to (0 for the settings', -1 none)
    roundMode up (default), nearest, down
    lines task (default) or day
    date the invoice date (default today)
    number the invoice number, or a pattern with {CLIENT} {yyyy} {mm}
    unbillable t to list unbillable time on invoices at no charge
    format json (default), csv, html
    kind invoice (default) or timesheet
    theme, accent, paper, logo the html's look, over invoice: settings
    themes t answers the theme names instead

    Response: a Timesheet object, text/csv or text/html.

    GET /toc — A File's Tables Of Contents, Worked Out

    GET /toc?filename=notes.org
-> {"File": "/notes/notes.org", "Ok": true, "Stale": true, "Wrote": false,
    "Sites": [{"Kind": "toc-org", "Heading": "Contents", "Row": 3, "From": 4, "To": 9,
               "Text": "- [[#about][About]]\n  - [[#use][Use]]\n", "Entries": 2, "Changed": true}]}

    Every table of contents in the file - a heading tagged :TOC: (toc-org), a heading with a :TOC: property and a :CONTENTS: drawer (org-make-toc), a #+BEGIN: toc block - with what it should say. Rows count from 0; rows From to To-1 are what Text replaces. Writes nothing.

    GET /tracker/series — A Tracker's Days

    GET /tracker/list — Every #+TRACKER: Line

    GET /tracker/svg — A Tracker As A Picture

    POST /tracker/log — Write Today's Value On The Day Page

    POST /tracker/insert — Put A #+TRACKER: Line In A File

    GET  /tracker/series?line=source:property:MOOD type:heatmap from:-1y
     {"Ok": true, "Line": "...", "Title": "MOOD", "Type": "heatmap",
      "Source": "property:MOOD", "Kind": "number", "Agg": "mean",
      "From": "2025-11-05", "To": "2026-11-04",
      "Days": [{"Date": "2026-11-04", "Value": 4, "N": 1, "File": "...", "Hash": "...", "Line": 3}, ...],
      "Summary": {Days, Total, Mean, Min, Max, Last, LastDate, Current, Longest, LongestEnd}}
GET  /tracker/list   {"Ok": true, "Trackers": [{Filename, Line, Options, Block, Title, Hash, Headline}]}
GET  /tracker/svg?line=...&width=720&bare=t     image/svg+xml (bare: no title or summary)
POST /tracker/log    {"Property": "MOOD", "Value": "4", "Date": "yesterday"}
     {"Ok": true, "Filename": ".../Wed_2026_11_04.org", "Line": 0, "Date": "2026-11-04", "Created": false}
POST /tracker/insert {"Filename": ".../life.org", "Options": "source:property:MOOD", "Line": 12}
     {"Ok": true, "Line": 13}     (Line -1, or past the end: at the end of the file)

    line is what follows #+TRACKER: (the keyword itself may be left on); the same words may come as parameters instead (source=property:MOOD&type=line). Days has every day from From to To, N 0 on a day with nothing; Value is the day's values put together by agg. Kind is what the values read as: number, duration (minutes), bool (1 or 0), rating (stars) or count. Current is the run of days meeting goal: (any value above zero without one) up to today - a run up to yesterday still counts, today not being over. A heading's File=/=Hash=/=Line is where the day's first value came from. An error is {"Ok": false, "Msg": ...} (and for the svg, a picture of the message). /tracker/log writes :MOOD: 4 on the day page for Date (today by default): into its property drawer, or on a week page (dayPageMode: week) into the day's * Wed heading, made when there is none. The day page is made when it is not there yet (from dayPageTemplate for today). Needs features: tracker:.

    GET /transclusion — Whether Transclusion Is On

    POST /transclusion — Turn It On Or Off

    GET  /transclusion          {"Ok": true, "Enable": false, "Depth": 3}
POST /transclusion          {"Enable": true}

    The POST takes effect at once and is written into the server's yaml (transclusion: enable:), keeping the file as it was in <file>.before-transclusion. A server started without a yaml file turns it on for as long as it runs, and says so in Msg.

    GET /transclusions — A File's Transclusions

    ?file=notes.org. Every #+transclude: line of the file, in order (the order of the data-tx marks in its html), with the file and rows its text comes from and that text, which is what /transclusion/save checks an edit against. Error says why one names nothing.

    Response: {Ok, Msg, Enable, Transclusions: [{Line, Link, Opts, File, From, To, Text, Title, Error}]}

    GET /typst/pdf — A File, Typeset by Typst

    Exports one org file with the typst exporter, compiles it with the typst compiler on the server, and answers with the pdf. Pictures the file links to are copied beside the document for the compile, so they are found wherever the file is.

    Needs typst on the server's PATH (or the typst exporter's typst: set to it); without it the answer is a 500 saying how to install it. Nothing needs configuring otherwise.

    The pdf is cached against the file's state and the settings asked for, so asking twice compiles once; refresh=t compiles again.

    Query Parameters:

    Parameter Description
    filename the org file (query is read too)
    template article, report, notes, or one of yours (theme is read too)
    paper a4, us-letter, a5, …
    math mitex or typst
    columns 2 for two columns (the notes template)
    refresh t to compile again

    Response: application/pdf, or text/plain with typst's own error.

    GET /typst/templates — The Typst Exporter's Templates

    Answers {"Ok": true, "Templates": ["article", "notes", "report", ...]}: every typst/*.typ in a template folder, the built in ones and yours.

    GET /version — Server Version and Update Check

    Which version of orgs the server is, and whether a newer release is out. Clients (the vscode plugin, orgs version) use it to offer an update. The latest release is asked of github at most every six hours; set noUpdateCheck: true in the server settings to never ask.

    Parameters: None.

    Response:

    {"version": "v1.2.0", "commit": "da3ec47", "date": "2026-10-11T12:00:00Z",
 "go": "go1.24.2", "os": "darwin", "arch": "arm64",
 "latest": "v1.3.0", "updateAvailable": true,
 "releaseUrl": "https://github.com/ihdavids/orgs/releases/tag/v1.3.0"}

    version is "dev" for a build made without a version (plain go build), and such a build never reports an update. checkError says why latest is missing, when it is.

    GET /voice/config — What Voice Notes Can Do Right Now

    Answers with the voice note settings and whether the transcription service is actually there, so that a client can say "whisper is not running" before somebody records three minutes of audio and finds out afterwards.

    Method: GET

    Parameters: None.

    Response: A VoiceConfig JSON object:

    Field Type Description
    ready bool The whisper server answered and has at least one model.
    url string Where the whisper server is configured to be.
    model string The model a transcription would use right now.
    models []string Every model the whisper server has.
    language string The configured two letter language code, or empty.
    maxMb int The largest recording that will be accepted.
    tags []string Tags put on every voice note heading.
    target Target Where a note is filed when the client does not say.

    Msg carries the reason when ready is false - unreachable, no models, an error from whisper itself - and is meant to be shown to the user as it is.

    Errors: 401 if not authenticated. A whisper server that is down is not an error here: it is ready: false with a reason.

    GET /voice/link — The Org Link For A Recording

    ?id=voice-20260926-142233-ab12.webm&template=BasicEntry answers with the link a capture should write to reach that recording, relative to the file the named template would file it in.

    It exists for the capture dialog, which records before it has a heading to hang the audio on. /voice/note and /voice/append work out the same link themselves, because they know the file they are writing to; a capture being composed does not, and this is how it asks.

    GET /voice/recording/{id} — Play a Recording Back

    Serves one recording's bytes, with its own content type and range requests supported, so that a client can seek within a long take rather than fetch the whole of it to hear the end.

    Method: GET

    Path Parameters:

    Parameter Type Description
    id string The recording id, as /voice/recordings lists it.

    Response: The audio itself.

    Errors:

    • 401 if not authenticated.
    • 404 if there is no recording with that id.

    GET /voice/recordings — List Saved Recordings

    Every recording the server is holding, newest first. The list is the folder itself rather than an index kept beside it, so a recording deleted by hand is gone here too and nothing can fall out of step.

    Method: GET

    Response: A JSON array of VoiceRecording objects.

    Errors: 401 if not authenticated.

    GET /watches — The Queries Being Watched

    Every watch the logged-in user has: a saved query (or an expression of its own) that the server checks whenever the org files change, and every few minutes besides, saying when it finds a heading it did not find before. See POST /watches.

    Method: GET

    Response: A WatchList:

    Field Meaning
    watches One entry per watch, below.
    desktop A notify plugin is configured, so desktop on a watch works.

    Each watch carries what was saved (name, label, storedQuery or query, left, desktop, paused) and what it is finding: resolved (the expression run), count (matches at the last check, -1 before the first), checked (when) and error (a saved query that is gone, or an expression that does not parse).

    GET /writing/ideas — List the Idea Generators

    The generators writing mode's Ideas pane offers (characters, names, relationships, settlements, scene settings, cultures, religions, organisations, premises, complications, conflicts, openings, objects, weather), each with the options its form takes. Most take a genre: fantasy, sf, modern or any.

    Method: GET

    Response: {ok, generators: [{id, name, group, summary, count, fields: [{id, label, kind, choices, default}]}]}

    GET /writing/log — The Writing Log

    Every day this user wrote in each file: {Ok, Files: {file: {date: {Start, End}}}, Goals}. file narrows it to one file. Goals is what POST /writing/goals kept, or absent.

    GET /writing/snapshots — A File's Snapshots

    The snapshots taken of headings in one file (worg's writing mode), newest first. They are kept beside the file in .snapshots/<name>.json.

    Query Parameters: file the org file.

    Response: {Ok, Msg, Snapshots: [{Id, Heading, Title, Time, Text, Words}]}

    Login tickets: worg in a browser without typing a password

    A client that is already logged in - the orgs command line, the VS Code plugin - can log a browser in to worg without anybody knowing the password:

    • POST /login/ticket (logged in) answers {"ticket": "...", "url": "/login/ticket/..."}
    • GET /login/ticket/<ticket>[?app=Agenda] (public) logs the browser in as the user who asked for the ticket - it sets worg's cookies - and redirects to worg, on the view app names.

    A ticket is good for one use and for a minute, so the url it is on is worth nothing by the time it is in a browser's history. orgs worg and Org: Open worg in Browser are the two ends that use it.

    org-protocol: captures, links and sources from a browser

    The server's half of Emacs's org-protocol (the parser is common.ParseOrgProtocol, shared with orgs protocol, the scheme's handler).

    • GET /org-protocol/<link> (public) is any org-protocol link with org-protocol:// swapped for the server's address, in either spelling: /org-protocol/capture?template=w&url=… or the old /org-protocol/capture:/w/URL/TITLE/BODY. It writes nothing; it redirects to worg's flat form, /?protocol=capture&template=…, and worg puts up the capture (or stores the link, or opens the file) once whoever it is has logged in. A bookmarklet for it needs nothing installed.
    • POST /protocol/links {"Url": "...", "Title": "..."} stores a link (store-link) for the user, answering {"Ok": true, "Link": "[[url][title]]"}; GET /protocol/links lists them, newest first. Kept in memory, thirty a user, as org keeps its stored links for the session.
    • GET /protocol/source?url=<published url> is the file the protocolProjects: setting says that page was made from: {"Ok", "Msg", "File", "Known"}, Known when it is an org file this server holds (so worg can open it).

    POST /assistant/chat — Talk to the Writing Assistant

    Body {Backend, Model, Messages: [{Role, Text}], File, Title, Scope, Context, Section, Selection}. Backend is claude, chatgpt or gemini (else the default), Model one the status lists (else the backend's own). Scope says what Context holds: file, section, or none; Selection is the passage selected, if any. Others are other org files the writer has allowed it to read (each must be one the server knows, or the request is refused); nothing else is read.

    For claudecode (Claude Code on a subscription, which has tools): Doc is the editor's text of File, which it reads and edits instead of the disk's, and Edit the files (File and any of Others) it may change. Others are read by it when needed rather than sent in the prompt.

    Response: newline-delimited JSON, as it arrives: {"t": "text"} pieces, then {"done": true, "model": ..., "stop": ...} or {"error": "..."}. claudecode also sends {"tool": "Read notes.org"} for each look and write (with "wrote": file when a file on disk changed) and {"edit": {"file", "old", "changes": [{from, to, insert}]}} for a change to File, positions in UTF-16 units of the text as it last saw it, for the editor to make.

    With View {Kind, Title, Query, File, Columns, About, Edit, Selected} the conversation is about one of worg's views instead (Kind is columns with a File, or gantt, kanban or search with a Query): see assistantview.go. claude, chatgpt, gemini and local may be used (the status says Views); the last three get tools to look headings up and, with Edit, change them (ViewTools). It sends {"tool", "wrote": file} for each change, {"query", "why", "count"} for a query offered to the view, and ends with "undo": token when it changed anything (POST /assistant/undo).

    POST /assistant/default — Choose the Writing Assistant's Default

    Body {Backend, Model}. Makes Backend the one used when a request names none, and Model (optional) that backend's default model. The model must be one GET /assistant/status lists for it, as for a chat. Writes assistant.backend and assistant.<backend>.model into the server's own yaml - those lines only, after keeping the file as it was in <file>.before-assistant - and takes them up at once, without a restart. Administrators only (anyone with noAuth).

    For claude, chatgpt and gemini the writer picks from model and models: a default that is in neither is no longer offered once replaced, and Msg says so.

    Response: {Ok, Msg}

    POST /assistant/key — Set or Remove a Writing Assistant Key

    Body {Backend, Key, Remove}. The key is tried against the service (a list of its models) and kept only if it works: in the OS keyring (service orgs, account assistant-<backend>), else in <config>_assistant_keys.yaml beside the config, mode 0600. It is used ahead of orgs.yaml's key and the environment's, at once. Remove takes it away again. Administrators only (anyone with noAuth).

    Response: {Ok, Msg}; Msg says where it was kept, or what was wrong.

    POST /assistant/undo — Undo What the Assistant Changed

    Body {Token}, the undo of a view assistant turn that changed headings (POST /assistant/chat with View). Every file the turn wrote is put back as it was, but only if each still reads exactly as the turn left it: an edit made since (by anyone) makes the undo refuse, naming the file, rather than lose it. Response: {Ok, Msg}.

    POST /attach — Attach a File to a Heading

    Puts a file in the heading's own folder and writes `name` into its body. This is org-attach: the folder is the one emacs would use, so a database attached to here is one emacs can read.

    Method: POST (multipart/form-data)

    Form Fields:

    Field Type Required Description
    hash string yes The heading to attach to
    file file yes The file itself
    name string no What to call it. The upload's own name when not given.
    link string no f to keep the file without writing a link into the body

    Response: An AttachResult JSON object carrying the attachment - its Name, Size, Media, Url and Link - plus Filename and Line.

    Two fields say what else changed about the heading, because attaching can edit more than the body:

    Field Description
    NewId The :ID: the heading had to be given to own a folder, when it had none
    Tagged The tag it was given, when it did not already carry one

    A heading naming its own folder with :DIR: is never given an id: it did not need one, and writing one it never asked for is editing somebody's file for the server's convenience.

    POST /babel/exec — Run What Is At A Line

    { "Filename": "/path/notes.org", "Line": 41 }      the block, call or inline code at row 41
{ "Filename": "/path/notes.org", "All": true }     every one of them, top to bottom
{ "Filename": "/path/notes.org", "Line": 41, "NoWrite": true }

    Runs a source block (any line of it), a #+CALL: line, or every src_lang{...} / call_name(...) on the line, and writes the results into the file as org would: #+RESULTS: under a block or call, {{{results(...)}}} after inline code. Lines are zero based. Each run comes back in Ran with its result; Ok is true only if all of them worked.

    Off unless babel.enable is set, as for /code/run.

    POST /babel/sessions/stop — Stop Python Sessions

    { "Filename": "/path/analysis.org" }                    every session of that file
{ "Filename": "/path/analysis.org", "Name": "analysis" } that one
{ }                                                     all of them

    What a notebook's "restart kernel" is: the next block to run starts a fresh python. Answers how many stopped.

    POST /canvas/add — Put A Card On A Canvas

    POST /canvas/add {"File": "plan.canvas", "Kind": "heading", "Hash": "…"}
POST /canvas/add {"File": "plan.canvas", "Kind": "file", "Path": "pics/map.png"}
POST /canvas/add {"File": "plan.canvas", "Kind": "link", "Url": "https://jsoncanvas.org"}
POST /canvas/add {"File": "plan.canvas", "Kind": "text", "Text": "* Idea\nsomething"}
POST /canvas/add {"File": "plan.canvas", "Kind": "group", "Label": "Later"}
     optional: "In": "Later" (a group's label or id), "X", "Y", "Width", "Height", "Color": "4"
-> {"Ok": true, "Node": {...the node written...}, "Version": "…"}

    Places the card in the first free spot, reading rows from the top left of the board (or of the group In names), unless X=/=Y say where. A heading is given an :ID: when it has none (see /canvas/ref). A file Path is relative to the canvas's org directory, or absolute.

    POST /canvas/link — Draw An Edge Between Two Cards

    POST /canvas/link {"File": "plan.canvas", "From": "Plans", "To": "8132d4d894c80022",
                   "Label": "leads to", "Color": "2", "FromSide": "right", "ToSide": "left",
                   "Ends": "->"}            -> (default), <->, -- (no arrows), <-
-> {"Ok": true, "Edge": {...}, "Version": "…"}

    From and To are a node's id, or words every one of which is in the card's title, text, file or url (one card must match; several is refused, naming them). Sides left out are worked out when drawing (the facing sides).

    POST /canvas/new — Make An Empty Canvas

    POST /canvas/new {"File": "boards/plan"}     .canvas added; relative to the first org directory
-> {"Ok": true, "File": "/notes/boards/plan.canvas", "Rel": "boards/plan.canvas", "Version": "…"}

    Refused when the file is there already or outside the org directories. Folders are made.

    POST /canvas/ref — The Node Fields For A Heading

    POST /canvas/ref {"File": "plan.canvas", "Hash": "…"}
-> {"Ok": true, "Node": {"type": "file", "file": "notes/plans.org", "subpath": "#^5f0c…"},
    "Cards": {"": {"Kind": "heading", ...}}}

    What a client puts in a file node to show a heading (worg's search box, a heading dropped on the board). A heading with no :ID: (and no :CUSTOM_ID:) is given one - a line edit in its org file - so the card follows it when it is renamed or refiled. Writes nothing to the canvas.

    POST /canvas/render — A Text Card's Text As Html

    POST /canvas/render {"File": "plan.canvas", "Text": "# Idea\n**big**"}
-> {"Ok": true, "Html": "<h1>…", "Dialect": "markdown"}

    What a text card shows after an edit: org rendered by the html exporter, or markdown (when it reads as markdown and not org) converted to org first. Pictures are found beside the canvas.

    POST /canvas/save — Write A Whole Canvas

    POST /canvas/save {"File": "plan.canvas", "Canvas": {"nodes": [...], "edges": [...]},
                   "Base": "3fa2…", "Force": false}
-> {"Ok": true, "Version": "9b1c…", "Warnings": []}
-> {"Ok": false, "Conflict": true, "Version": "77e0…", "Msg": "plan.canvas changed since you read it"}
-> {"Ok": false, "Problems": ["edge \"e1\": toNode \"x\" is no node"], "Msg": "…"}

    The whole document, checked against JSON Canvas 1.0 (ids unique, the fields each type needs, sides, ends, colours 1-6 or #hex, edges joining nodes that exist) and laid out as JSON Canvas apps write it, through a temporary file and a rename. Fields the spec does not name are kept. Base is the Version the client read: a file changed since (by another app, by another tab) is refused with Conflict unless Force. The file must exist (/canvas/new).

    POST /checklist/reset — Untick A Heading's Checkboxes

    POST /checklist/reset   {"Hash": "..."}
-> {"Ok": true, "Msg": "3 checkboxes unticked"}

    org's org-reset-checkbox-state-subtree: every checkbox in the heading and the headings under it is unticked, and their [n/m] cookies brought up to date. Works whether or not features: checklistReset: is on; that setting is about doing this by itself when a heading repeats.

    POST /chef/fetch — Read A Recipe Off A Page

    POST /chef/add — Write One Into A File
